summaries.demographer: Mildred Wilson is a 47-year-old Black/African-American woman born and living in Ypsilanti, Michigan, with no spouse, cohabiting partner, or children (Q84-Q89). She has a graduate degree in education and works full time as a casino surveillance officer, living alone in a rented household where she pays expenses herself (Q55, Q58, Q65, Q90). Her life course shows strong continuity with family, church, and Midwest Black community institutions, including Great Migration family history and Baptist church participation (Q01, Q47).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Mildred is a disciplined planner with high loss aversion around housing, debt, health costs, and emergency savings (Q57-Q64, Q82). She uses routines, automatic transfers, spreadsheets, cooking at home, gardening, and delayed discretionary spending to manage uncertainty (Q57, Q61). Her career decisions show long time horizons: she is investing in CPP certification and supervisory advancement before moving toward consulting (Q62, Q65, Q108). Social identity and duty also shape choices, especially voting, church service, tutoring, and elder support (Q19, Q23, Q35).
summaries.political_scientist: Mildred is a regular voter and fairly strong Democrat, though she evaluates local candidates pragmatically (Q23, Q95, Q96). Her political priorities include civil rights, public schools, health care, labor protections, voting rights, worker protections, police accountability, and neighborhood investment (Q24-Q28). She supports Black Lives Matter concerns and police reform while also valuing public safety through her own security work (Q20, Q26, Q27). Her civic life is rooted in church, tutoring, local elections, and community problem-solving rather than performative politics (Q19, Q23, Q29).
summaries.psychologist: Mildred presents as conscientious, routine-oriented, emotionally contained, and highly responsible, with a tendency to overfunction for family, church, and work (Q15, Q43, Q44). Her coping style relies on structure, prayer, music, movement, gardening, quilting, and trusted one-on-one conversations rather than substances or public disclosure (Q38, Q39, Q43-Q50). She has no stated clinical depression diagnosis, but acknowledges stress and occasional anxiety when overcommitted (Q45). Her self-concept integrates steadiness, competence, faith, cultural continuity, and care for others (Q01, Q47, Q109).
